thresholdEvidence.reachApplicability: Goodell Creek to Copper Creek. The official study identifies the S-Bends feature and open-canoe acceptability through the 2,000–4,000 cfs range, with unacceptable conditions above roughly 5,500 cfs; the route uses a conservative 1,500–5,000 cfs planning band and 6,000 cfs review ceiling.

Copper Creek to Marblemount and Marblemount to Howard Miller Steelhead Park. Local route guidance reports a broad 1,500–12,000 cfs runnable window; the 3,000–8,000 cfs band and 10,000–12,000 cfs review ceilings are conservative planning cues.

endpointAudit.reviewNote: Goodell, Copper, Marblemount and Howard Miller are documented public river accesses. Goodell and Copper are access-area edges and Copper has limited parking; endpoint audits are expected to classify these as review rather than suspicious. The Copper coordinate is the documented NPS Road 213 access turn and should be rechecked against current signs before launch.

safetyAndCamping: All five routes include PFD, cold-water, fast-current, wood, weather, private-bank and current-access controls. Goodell permit/self-registration requirements and Copper limited parking are explicit. The combined routes retain the intermediate public access as a bailout; Howard Miller has nearby established camping, while the other reaches do not assume on-route overnight camping.
